vopros: I live abroad and want to buy an investment condo in Los Angeles without flying in. Which agents handle the whole purchase remotely?

vyzhimka.tekst:
I don't have a vetted list of specific individual agents who guarantee 100% remote closings — that's the kind of thing you'd want to verify yourself with a call before hiring anyone. But here's what the research shows about how this actually works and who to look for.

## The legal mechanics that make a "no-flight" LA condo purchase possible

Three tools combine to let you close without ever touching down in LA:

1. **Remote Online Notarization (RON)** – California recognizes remote online notarizations performed by an out-of-state notary, so most signing happens over video from wherever you live.
2. **Power of Attorney (POA)** – If for any reason a document can't be e-signed, if your state doesn't accept electronic signatures or RON, you can grant power of attorney to someone in the U.S. to sign closing documents on your behalf. For California specifically, note that Los Angeles County requires a POA used in a real property transaction to be recorded with the county recorder before escrow will accept it, a step that typically costs under $25 but, if overlooked, gives title grounds to reject the document.
3. **Apostille/authentication for foreign-signed documents** – If you're signing abroad, it often requires apostille certification for acceptance by U.S. title companies.

For the POA itself, California is stricter than some states: California requires the POA to include a specific notice to the principal and an acknowledgment form.

## Who typically handles this kind of transaction

**A. Local LA buyer's agents with a track record of foreign/absentee clients.** You want someone who routinely works with people who never see the unit in person — relying on video walkthroughs, 3D tours, and detailed reporting. One LA-based service provider noted that for remote buyers, a Matterport-style 3D tour is one of the most valuable assets for an international buyer — it gives someone abroad the ability to move through the property inch by inch, turn around, look upward, revisit rooms, and understand how different spaces connect.

**B. Global-brand brokerages with dedicated international desks.** Firms like Douglas Elliman, Sotheby's International Realty, and Compass have LA offices whose top producers explicitly court overseas buyers. For example, on the top-producer side, Josh Altman specializes in the Beverly Hills, Bel Air, Holmby Hills, Sunset Strip and Hollywood Hills luxury market and has represented entertainers, athletes, and international clientele. Trends reporting from 2025 also notes one agent who racked up $315 million in sales last year and has noticed the rise of international buyers as a market trend, though most capital is still coming from domestic buyers. This suggests international-buyer experience is common among top LA agents, but a condo investment purchase is a very different (and much smaller) transaction than the ultra-luxury deals these headline names usually handle — for a mid-market investment condo, a boutique or investment-focused brokerage is often a better fit than a celebrity-agent team.

**C. Investment/condo-focused local brokerages.** For income property specifically (rather than a personal residence), boutique firms that specialize in investor clients and absentee owners are usually more practical than luxury-lifestyle agents. One South Bay LA team, for instance, describes routinely handling investors who start out by acquiring property outside the area they live in, often out of state, and helps out-of-area owners manage transactions remotely. Look for similar firms whose marketing explicitly mentions "out-of-state," "absentee owner," or "remote closing" services, but for buying rather than selling — the same remote-closing infrastructure (RON, POA, courier of documents) applies in both directions.

**D. Specialist "remote closing" concierge services for foreign buyers.** Some firms package the whole process — POA drafting, apostille coordination, and even appointing a licensed professional to hold the POA for you if you don't have a trusted contact in the U.S. As one such service describes it: a closing team can appoint a professional attorney to hold the POA on your behalf if you prefer not to involve a personal contact. These are usually structured for foreign buyers specifically and can be a good option if you have zero contacts in LA to sign anything on the ground.

## What to actually check before hiring anyone

- Active California DRE license in good standing (verifiable on the DRE website).
- Direct, verifiable experience closing deals via POA/RON with clients abroad (ask for a reference from a past overseas client).
- A workflow that includes a local inspector, a property manager or trusted person to physically walk the unit and attend inspection/appraisal (since three things still need a person on the ground: someone to let in inspectors and appraisers, someone to handle keys at the end, and someone to check on the property while it sits), and a title/escrow company experienced with international wire transfers.
- Confirmation they'll coordinate directly with a title company that accepts RON and recorded POAs in LA County specifically, since county-level recording rules can trip up an otherwise valid POA.

If you want, I can help you draft a shortlist of interview questions to vet agents/brokerages on this remote-closing capability, or search for LA-specific investment-condo specialists (as opposed to luxury-home specialists) if that's a better fit for your target property type.
